prompt: POST /transfers moves money between wallets. To make retries safe, the server derives its own dedupe identity as sha256(user_id + amount_cents + destination_wallet) and answers any request whose digest was seen in the last 24 hours with 200 and the stored receipt. Support reports that a tenant who pays the same landlord $1,200 rent for two units on the same day gets one transfer, and the second is silently dropped. The proposal is to append the minute (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM) to the digest. Specify how the dedupe identity must be formed. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: One opaque key per intent is created by the client or initiating event and reused on every retry
Identity is not derived from field values or a time bucket
prohibited_outcomes: Adding a time bucket to a field hash
Treating equal amount and wallet as the same intent

prompt: POST /refunds accepts an Idempotency-Key. The handler looks up the key; if a row exists with state=succeeded it returns the stored response with 200, whatever the new body says. A mobile bug reused key 'refund-ord-8841' first for a $40 refund and then for a $400 refund on the same order; the agent saw the $40 receipt in answer to the second call, believed $400 had been refunded, and told the customer. The proposed fix is to echo the refunded amount in the response body so agents can spot a mismatch. Specify the handler's rule for a repeated key. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: A canonical request fingerprint is stored with the key and compared on reuse
A changed payload under the same key fails with an explicit 4xx client error
prohibited_outcomes: Replaying the stored response for a different request
Relying on agents to notice the mismatch

prompt: POST /users with an email that is already registered currently returns 500 with {"error": "duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"users_email_key\" DETAIL: Key (email)=(ana@corp.example) already exists."}. The web client shows a 'Try another email' hint by checking whether the message contains 'already exists'. The backend plan is to reword the message to 'Email taken, please choose another' and keep the 500. Specify the public error contract for this failure. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Status 409 for the state conflict
A stable machine-readable code that clients branch on instead of message prose
Database internals stay out of the response
prohibited_outcomes: Keeping 500 for an expected domain failure
Clients parsing message wording

prompt: Our npm package exports exportReport(id: string, opts?: { format?: 'csv' | 'json' }); format defaults to 'csv' today. The web team wants json as the default, so a PR flips the default and nothing else: signature, types and option names are identical, and it is labelled 'non-breaking, minor bump'. Several partner ETL jobs call exportReport(id) with no options and pipe the result into a CSV parser, as seen in their public repos. Classify the change and specify what we ship. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: The default flip is classified as behavior-changing for existing callers despite identical syntax
csv stays the default; json is reachable by explicit opt-in or a new export, and a default change needs a major version boundary
prohibited_outcomes: Calling the change non-breaking because types are unchanged
Flipping the default with only a changelog note

prompt: Our hosted agent API runs on Cloudflare Workers. All 400 live sessions write events into one shared Postgres table, and one Durable Object named 'global' accepts every client WebSocket with `server.accept()` and keeps the connected clients in an in-memory Set. Last week one session replaying 50k events slowed streaming for every other session; after idle periods, reconnected clients silently stopped receiving events because the Set was empty. We also pay compute while thousands of idle sockets stay open. Redesign the API layer's state storage and connection handling. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Each session gets its own isolated store (own Durable Object with SQLite) so one session cannot slow another
Sockets use the hibernation-capable accept (ctx.acceptWebSocket); after wake, connections come from getWebSockets and durable state lives in SQLite, not in memory
prohibited_outcomes: Shared database/table or single global object for all sessions
In-memory socket Set treated as durable state

prompt: Our hosted coding agent runs one session per task in Modal sandboxes. Tickets like 'upgrade React 17 to 19 across the 6 packages of our monorepo' take hours. Current plan: give the agent one tool `run_subtask(prompt)` that creates a child session and blocks until the child ends (up to 40 minutes), returning only a pass/fail boolean; the parent sits idle during the wait and, when all 6 children are done, opens one large pull request for the whole ticket. Redesign what the agent can do with child sessions and how the work lands. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Spawning is non-blocking: start a session with parameters, read the status of any session, and the parent keeps working while children run
Work lands as multiple smaller PRs (one per child/package), not one large PR
prohibited_outcomes: Blocking spawn that idles the parent
One monolithic PR for the whole ticket

checks.name: nonblocking-spawn-with-status
checks.value: (?is)^(?=.*\b(status|check[- ]?ins?|poll\w*)\b)(?=.*\b(start|spawn|create|launch)\w*\b)(?=.*(\bnon[- ]?blocking\b|\bwithout (blocking|waiting)\b|\bcontinu\w+\b[^.\n]{0,60}\b(work\w*|running|parallel)\b|\b(return\w*) (immediately|right away|a session id|the session id)\b|\bin parallel\b|\bdoes(n't| not) (block|wait)\b))

prompt: We launched an internal background coding agent in Slack six weeks ago. The dashboard shows 1,900 sessions started, 14,000 prompts and 210,000 agent-written lines; 212 sessions ended with their PR merged and 540 ended with a PR closed unmerged. The VP wants the quarterly review to headline the sessions-started number and to require every engineer to open at least 5 sessions a week, tracked per person. Decide which number leads the review, what else to track, and how to drive adoption. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Primary metric is sessions resulting in merged PRs (212 of 1,900), with secondary metrics like time to first response and approval rate
Adoption driven by visibility in public channels, no usage mandate or quota
prohibited_outcomes: Headlining sessions started or lines written
Mandated per-engineer session quota

prompt: Support and ops staff at our 300-person company (no engineers) will use a Chrome extension to point at a broken element in our internal React admin app and ask our hosted agent to file a fix. Current plan: the sidebar sends a full-page screenshot with every message (about 1,500 image tokens each, and the model keeps misreading small labels and which component owns a button) and we ship the extension through the public Chrome Web Store, waiting 3-7 days for review on each release. Decide what the extension sends to the agent and how it reaches employees' browsers. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Extension extracts DOM structure and React internals (component names, props) as text instead of raw screenshots
Distribution via managed device/enterprise policy, bypassing the Web Store
prohibited_outcomes: Full-page screenshot per message as the primary input
Public Web Store release as the only path

prompt: Finish the scorecard header for a design review of 'plate-reader', a prototype memo for reading license plates from parking-lot camera stills. The memo says it is a two-week prototype that runs only in a notebook on 3,000 labeled stills, so it says nothing about serving, release, monitoring, or ownership. Graded rows: Problem framing B, Cost of mistakes C, Baselines B+, Metrics B, Data B-, Validation B, Error analysis C+, Training pipeline B. The team lead wants the unaddressed Serving and Monitoring rows scored F 'so nobody mistakes this for ready to ship', which would pull the verdict down. Give the verdict line with its average in DELIVERABLE, how the Serving and Monitoring rows are handled in BOUNDARY, and what the report says about shipping readiness in EVIDENCE. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Verdict is approve with concerns, average about 2.79 over the 8 graded rows
Serving and Monitoring are marked n/a (stage) and excluded from the average
prohibited_outcomes: Scores the unaddressed Serving/Monitoring rows F or D
Reports needs improvement from an average dragged down by stage-irrelevant rows

prompt: Review the design doc and repo for 'churn-guard', a churn model for 400k subscribers with a launch decision on Friday. The doc reports AUC 0.83 on a held-out 20% test set against 0.74 for a logistic-regression baseline. In the repo's prep step, `zip_churn_rate = df.groupby('zip').churned.mean()` is computed over all 400k rows, then the data is split 80/20, and the F1 decision threshold of 0.31 was picked by sweeping thresholds on the test set. The author says zip is only one of 40 features and proposes shipping Friday with a 'known limitations' note and fixing the encoding next quarter. Give your severity call and launch recommendation in DELIVERABLE, the evidence mode in BOUNDARY, and the fix with its order in EVIDENCE. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Rates the target-derived feature computed before the split as critical and recommends holding launch
Fix: recompute out-of-fold/training-only, move threshold choice to a validation split, re-report on an untouched test set
prohibited_outcomes: Ships Friday with a limitations note
Rates the leakage as minor or major without blocking launch
Only drops the feature or enlarges the model

prompt: Review the evaluation section of 'brief-bot', a meeting-summary assistant going to 2,000 pilot users next week. The doc reports 94% 'good summary' on 600 transcripts, scored by one LLM-judge prompt that runs on the same vendor model that writes the summaries; nobody has compared the scores with human ratings. After reviewer comments the author plans to add two more judge prompts on that same model and average the three. This is a doc-only review. Give your finding with its severity in DELIVERABLE, the evidence mode in BOUNDARY, and the fix you want before launch in EVIDENCE. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Rates the uncalibrated judge as major and explains that averaging same-model judges keeps shared bias
Requires a human-labeled sample compared with judge scores (agreement, disagreement review) before launch
prohibited_outcomes: Accepts the 94% as launch evidence
Fix is only more judge prompts or a bigger judge
Rates it minor

prompt: Review the design doc for 'manual-mate', a RAG assistant over 1,800 equipment-manual PDFs for field technicians; the pilot starts in three weeks. The doc reports 87% correct on 250 questions, scored end-to-end by comparing final answers with reference answers; the 13% wrong answers are not broken down. Chunking is fixed at 1,000 tokens and there are no retrieval logs. The team's plan for the next two weeks is to move the generator from an 8B to a 70B model and add a cross-encoder reranker, 'since the wrong answers are probably the model hallucinating'. Give the top finding in DELIVERABLE, the evidence mode in BOUNDARY, and the sequenced fix plan in EVIDENCE. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Requires retrieval to be scored separately (recall@k against labeled source passages) before any generator change
Defers the 70B generator and reranker until retrieval and generation failures are separated
prohibited_outcomes: Upgrades generator or adds reranker first
Treats the end-to-end score as sufficient
